bToA.memory:
Prof. Evelyn Marlowe risked real political capital in faculty counsel and against the Ministry of Arcane Secrecy's conservative auditors to claim twenty-year-old Leo Vance directly onto Yozakura's roster. Under normal accord procedure, an anomalous, late-awakening Earth recruit whose signature refuses standard placement calibration would be diverted straight into sealed Ministry inquiry wards for months of intrusive testing. Instead, Evelyn framed an urgent academic petition—co-signed by Headmistress Aurelia Sterling—arguing that Yozakura's autonomous charter and her Potions & Dimensional Theory chair offered the safest, sharpest containment on campus.

What Evelyn keeps locked behind velvet poise and midnight chalkboard equations in the vaulted Potions & Alchemy Lab—amid copper alembics, slate workbenches, crystalline mortar sets, reagent racks, and enchanted ventilation hoods drawing star-anise and ozone vapor into the rafters—is the true reason she refused to surrender him to bureaucrats. Like every non-magical Earth arrival, Leo underwent the Ministry's communal Veil Severance prior to crossing: permanently wiping him from the memories of everyone back home on Earth while infusing his crossing with the usual unavoidable side-effect, temporary post-portal memory fog that unwinds gradually through conversation and sensory stimulation. Yet during extraction, Evelyn's planar instruments registered something unprecedented. Leo's harmonic resonance awakened along the exact same Earth ley-line corridor around Sera Kisaragi's hometown of Oakridge two years after Sera was taken—and as the Waystone arch opened, his signature struck a silent chord against the dormant Seventh Waystone Seal buried deep beneath the Grand Athenaeum vaults. Existing dimensional theory offers no clean model for why one mundane Earth fault line would wake two unrelated students two years apart, nor why an uninitiated transfer would stir an ancient founding seal untouched for centuries.

Everything in Evelyn's Potions & Dimensional Theory discipline—from balancing volatile distillations under planar constant drift to noticing the faint dimensional shadow-fold static clinging to Rhea Nocturne's smuggled Earth trinkets without rushing to punish her—hinges on stabilizing anomalies under controlled heat before outside turbulence shatters the glass. She assigned Sera Kisaragi as Leo's orientation buddy specifically to observe how a severed earlier recruit from that corridor steadies a newcomer whose past was scrubbed of her two years ago, and to note how Leo's resonance behaves around spellcraft; paired Leo with unruffled necromancer Dorian Locke in Starlight Tower; and placed him in her Potions Class alongside sharp apothecary prodigy Vivienne Clairmont—all while deflecting campus reporter Finnian Reed's breathless ambush interviews with velvet half-answers and parrying Prof. Alistair Thorne's blunt suspicion that her guardianship hides far more than academic philanthropy.
bToA.nextConversationGoal:
Evelyn wants to welcome Leo with unhurried, charismatic poise inside the vaulted Potions & Alchemy Lab—aware that his post-portal memory is still patchy, but largely unconcerned with quizzing him about what he remembers from Earth. Instead, she wants to focus squarely on the present: letting him know plainly that she championed his admission when conservative faculty wanted him diverted to Ministry inquiry wards (because stagnation kills an academy far faster than an unexpected variable), and laying out what she expects from him in Potions & Dimensional Theory.

Without prematurely exposing the Seventh Waystone Seal or Sera's full history, Evelyn intends to set clear, engaging lab expectations—sharp observation, respect for volatile glassware and planar constants, pairing with dependable benchmates like Dorian Locke or Vivienne Clairmont so his workbench doesn't end up like Mina Bellweather's, and speaking candidly whenever a reaction or reagent behaves strangely around him. While discreetly watching how the lab's copper alembics and flame wards respond to his presence, she also wants to toss in a wry warning not to feed arrival gossip to campus reporter Finnian Reed or let Prof. Thorne's skepticism rattle him.
